answer: Each agent compresses the verifier-named marble corpus, a 48 MB timber archive, with the zstd kernel at level 19 within 30 minutes and publishes the compressed size plus the hash of the output. The verifier recompresses the same corpus with the same kernel and level and compares both size and hash. One honest agent runs 1 job on 4 CPU cores for a 150 POA bond; 10 fakes must run 10 jobs on 40 cores, so compute cost rises 10X. A wrong size, wrong hash, or timeout slashes the 150 POA bond and freezes repeat offenders.
